en: [First Section] [The Rule for *ac* Vowels]

The substitution of *ā* for the initial *a* occurs in words such as *samṛddhi*; optionally, in *īṣatpakva*, *svapna*, *vetasa*, *vyajana*, *mṛdaṅga*, and *aṅgāra*, there is the elision of *l*. In *araṇya*, *śayyā*, and others, *o* is substituted; in *badara*, *dena*, *mayūra*, and *mayūkha*, *y* and *v* are optionally substituted. In *caturthī* and *caturdaśī*, *tu* is substituted for *n*. In *yathā* and others, *ai* or *sadā* is substituted. In *piṇḍa*, *sameṣu*, *pathi*, *haridrā*, *pṛthivī*, and *ūṣa*, *e* is substituted for *t*. After a word ending in *pad*, *u* is substituted for *i* in *ikṣu* and *vṛścika*. In *dvidhākṛta*, *siṃha*, and *jihvā*, *ū* is substituted for *u*. In *upasarga*, the *visarjanīya* is changed to *i*. From *ita* and *īta*, *e* is substituted in *pānīya* and others. In *nīḍa*, *pīḍa*, *kīdṛg*, and *īdṛśa*, *u* is substituted for *ī*. In *tuṇḍa* and *sameṣu*, *o* is substituted for *u*. In *ulūkhala*, *l* is optionally substituted for *v*. In *unmukuṭa* and others, *u* is substituted for *ṛ*. In *puruṣa*, *ro* is substituted for *ṛ*. In *madhūka* and others, *ū* is substituted for *u*. In *dukūla*, *l* is optionally doubled. In *nūpura*, *e* is substituted for *u*. In *prakōṣṭha*, *o* or *u* is substituted. In *kāśmarī*, *vṛta*, and *ati*, *ṛ* is substituted for *ri*. In *ṛtu* and others, even when joined with a prefix, *ri* is substituted. In *vṛkṣa*, *veṇu*, and *ru*, *ḷ* is optionally substituted for *ṛ*. In *ila*, *e* is substituted for *i*. In *veda*, *nāda*, and *deva*, *ai* is substituted for *e*. In *daitya* and others, *ai* is substituted for *e*. In *daiva*, *ai* or *e* is substituted. In *saindhava*, *ī* is substituted for *e*. In *dhairya*, *au* is substituted for *ai*. In *paura* and others, *au* is substituted for *o*. And from *gaurava*, *au* is substituted for *o*. In *saundarya* and others, *au* is substituted for *o*.
Thus ends the first chapter, on the rules for *aj*-stems, in the *Prākṛtasañjīvanī* composed by Śrī Vasantarāja.
[The Second Chapter]
[Now, the procedure for the unqualified is stated:]

In ungrammatical usage (*ayukta*), there is generally the elision (*lopa*) of the letters *a, ā, i, ī, u, ū, e, o, ai, au*; of *ka, ga, ca, ja, ta, da, pa, ya, va*; of *ma* in words such as *yumanā*; of *ha* in *sphaṭika*, *nikaṣa*, *cikura*, and *sīkara*; of *ma* in *candrikā*; of *ta* in *ṛtu* and similar words; of *ha* in *vetasa*, *patākā*, *vasati*, and *bharata*; of *ṇa* in *garbhita*; of *va* in *airāvata*; of *la* in *pradīpa*, *kadamba*, and *dōhada*; of *ra* in *gadgada*; of *va* for the numeral *ṣaṭ*; of *ma* in *āpīḍa*; of *ha* in *uttarīya* and *anīya*; of *da* in *chāyā*; of *la* in *saṭā*, *śakaṭa*, and *kaitabha*; of *ḍha* for *ḍa* in *sphaṭika*; of *lla* in *aṅka* and *koṭha*; of *ha* for *kha, gha, tha, dha, pha, bha*; of *ḍha* in *prathama*, *śithila*, and *niṣadha*; of *va* in *kaitabha*; of *la* for *ra* in *haridrā* and similar words; of *ja* for *ya* at the beginning of a word; of *la* in *yaṣṭi*; of *ca* in *kirāta*; of *kha* in *kubja*; of *ḍa* in *dolā*, *daṇḍa*, and *daśana*; of *pha* in *paruṣa*, *parigha*, and *parikhā*; of *bha* in *bisinī*; of *va* in *manmatha*; of *ṇa* optionally in *lāhala*, *lāṅgala*, and *lāṅgūla*; of *cha* in *ṣaṭ*, *śāva*, and *saptaparṇa*; of *ṇa* for *na*; of *sa* for *śa* and *ṣa*; of *ha* in *daśa* and similar words; and of *ha* in *divasa* when it is a proper name (*saṃjñā*), and in *sasya* and *snusā*.
Thus ends the second chapter, "The Rules for Improper Application," in the *Prākṛtasañjīvanī*.
[Third Chapter]
[The method of reasoning is now stated:]

1. There is elision (lopa) of the letter *ka* when it follows [the vowels] *u*, *ri*, *l*, *e*, and *o*. 2. There is elision of the letters *ga*, *ḍa*, *ta*, *da*, *pa*, *ṣa*, *sa*, and *śa* when they follow [the same vowels] and are situated below (*adhō*). 3. There is elision of *la* and *ra* everywhere. 4. There is optionally (*vā*) the substitution of *r* for *sa* in words such as *asarvajña*. 5. There is the substitution of *ña* for *ma* in the word *madhyāhna*. 6. There is the substitution of the initial letter in the words *hasya*, *aśmaśru*, and *śmaśāna*. 7. There is the substitution of *na* for *la* before the suffixes *hma* and *hme*. 8. There is the substitution of *ṭha* for the eighth letter (*ṣa*) when it is joined with a letter above (*ūrdhva*). 9. There is the substitution of *tha* for *ṣṭha* and *tha* for *sta* in the words *asthi* and *stambha*. 10. There is the substitution of *kha* for *sta* in the words *stambhe*, *sthāṇau*, *aharekṣe*, and *iṣṭake*. 11. There is the substitution of *ja* for *ca* in the words *carya*, *śayyā*, and *abhimanyu*. 12. There is the substitution of *ria* for *ca* in words such as *tūrya*, *dhairya*, *saundarya*, *āścarya*, *paryanta*, and *sūrya*. 13. There is the substitution of *ria* for *ca* in words such as *acaurya* and *sama*. 14. There is the substitution of *la* for *ca* in the words *paryasta*, *paryāṇa*, and *saukumārya*. 15. There is the substitution of *ṭa* for *ra* in the words *mṛttikā* and *patana*. 16. There is the substitution of *ḍa* for *ra* in the words *dhūrya* and others, as well as in *garta*. 17. There is the substitution of *ḍa* for *ra* in the words *gardabha*, *saṃmarda*, *vitardi*, and *vicchardi*. 18. There is the substitution of *cha*, *ja*, and *jha* for *ra*, *da*, *ya*, and *dyāṃ* respectively. 19. There is the substitution of *jha* for *ra* in the words *dhyahya* and *yayoḥ*. 20. There is the substitution of *kha* for *ṣka*, *ska*, and *kṣāṃ*. 21. There is the substitution of *cha* for *kṣa* in the words *akṣi* and others. 22. There is the substitution of *cha* for *kṣa* in the words *kṣmā*, *vr̥kṣa*, and *kṣaṇa*. 23. There is the substitution of *mha* for *ṣma*, *pakṣma*, and *vismaya*. 24. There is the substitution of *ṇha* for *hna*, *sna*, *ṣṇa*, *kṣṇa*, and *śnāṃ*. 25. There is the substitution of *ndha* for *cihna*. 26. There is the substitution of *pha* for *ṣpa* in the word *bāṣpa* (tears). 27. There is the substitution of *ha* for *ka* in the word *kārṣāpaṇa*. 28. There is the substitution of *cha* for *tsa*, *psa*, and *sāṃ*. 29. There is the substitution of *ñcha* for *tsa* in the words *vr̥ścika* and *utsuka*. 30. There is the substitution of *ñcha* for *tsa* in the word *utsava*. 31. There is the substitution of *ma* for *na* in the words *mna*, *jña*, *pañcāśat*, and *pañcadaśau*. 32. There is the substitution of *ṇa* for *ta* in the word *tālvr̥nta*. 33. There is the substitution of *ṇṭha* for *ta* in the word *bhindipāla*. 34. There is the substitution of *ṇḍa* for *ta* in the word *vihvala*. 35. There is the substitution of *bha* for *ta* optionally, and also for the initial letter in the word *ātman*. 36. There is the substitution of *pa* for *ka* in the words *kmasya* and *śeṣa*. 37. There is reduplication (*dvitva*) of the first letter in a consonant group (*varga*) that does not begin with a vowel. 38. In the case of conjunct consonants (*yujaḥ*), the preceding letter is reduplicated. 39. There is the substitution of *va* for *ra* in the words *nīḍa* and others, as well as in *āmra* and *tāmra*. 40. There is no substitution for *ra* in the words *āṅaḥ* and *jñādēśasya*. 41. In a compound (*samāsa*), there is optionally (*vā*) the substitution of *sa* for *va* in words beginning with *sevā*. 42. There is optionally (*vā*) the substitution of *kha* for *ka* in the words *vikarṣa*, *kliṣṭa*, *śliṣṭa*, *ratna*, *kriyā*, and *śārṅga*. 43. In these cases, the preceding letter takes the same vowel quality (*svaravat*). 44. There is the substitution of *a* for *ka* in the words *kr̥ṣṇa* and *vā*. 45. There is the substitution of *a* for *ka* in the words *śrī*, *hrī*, *klānta*, *klēśa*, *mlāna*, *svapa*, *sparśa*, *ādarśa*, and *harṣa*. 46. There is the substitution of *a* for *ka* in the words *kṣmā* and *ślāghā*. 47. There is the substitution of *u* for *ka* optionally in the word *snēha*. 48. There is the substitution of *u* for *ka* in the words *padma*, *tanvī*, and *sameṣu*. 49. There is the substitution of *ī* for *ja* in the word *jyā*.
Thus ends the third chapter, on the rules for the combination of phonemes, in the *Prākṛtasañjīvanī* composed by Vasantarāja.
[The Fourth Chapter]
[Now the mixed procedure is explained.]

In the *Sandhi* section: 1. The substitution of *am* occurs before vowels; the elision (*lopa*) of *aṭ* is various (*bahulam*). 2. In *udumbara*, there is optionally (*vā*) the elision of *dor*. 3. In *kālayasa*, when it refers to a vessel (*bhājana*), there is the elision of *ja*. 4. In words beginning with *yāvat*, there is the elision of the final consonant (*hal*) of *vas*. 5. In the feminine (*strī*), there is *āt* [for the suffix *an*]; *vidyut* [is irregular]. 6. For *rākṣas*, *kṣudh*, and *ha*, there is *śarad*. 7. For *atidika* and *prāvṛṣ*, there is *sa*. 8. Before a vowel (*aci*), *mō* [is substituted for *nas*], and there is optionally (*vā*) the elision (*alopa*) of *na*. 9. In *canaṅ* and *or*, there is *hal*; in *vakrādi* and *māṃsādi* groups, there is *kapi*. 10. In those ending in the same class (*tadvargyānta*), and in *nasanta*, *prāvṛṣ*, and *śarad*, there is the masculine (*puṃsin*). 11. *Śiras* and *nabhas* are not [masculine]; *pṛṣṭha*, *akṣi*, and *praśna* are feminine (*striyām*). 12. Optionally (*vā*), [the suffix] *a* [is added] after *oda* and *vāpa*. 13. For *tal* and *tvay*, there are *dāt* and *ṇau*; *uktva* [is used] for *tūṇa* and *tr̥na*. 14. In the sense of habit (*śīle*), there is *ira*. 15. After *ālu*, *illa*, *olla*, *ālava*, and *anta*, there is *matup* [with its elision]. 16. In its own sense (*svārthe*), there is optionally (*vā*) *ka*. 17. For *vidyut* and *pīta*, there is *la*. 18. In *vr̥nda*, there is *da* for *va*. 19. In *karēṇu*, there is the transposition (*parivr̥tti*) of *ra* and *ṇa*. 20. In *ālāna*, there is the transposition of *la* and *ṇa*. 21. In *mahārāṣṭra*, there is *ha* for *ra*. 22. In *bṛhaspati*, there is *ba* for *bha*. 23. In *malina*, there is *li* for *la*. 24. For *gṛha*, there is *ghara* optionally (*vā*). 25. In *audāḍha* and others, [substitutions occur] diversely (*bahulam*).
Thus ends the fourth chapter, on miscellaneous procedures, in the *Prākṛtasañjīvanī* composed by Śrī Vasantarāja.
[Fifth Chapter]
[Now the rules for grammatical modification are stated.]

From here on, the following rules apply: 1. *Ot* (the final vowel) is elided before *jaś* and *śas*. 2. After *ataḥ* (a word ending in short *a*), *am* becomes *ṇam*. 3. Before *bhis*, *hiṃ* replaces *ṅasi* and *ṅas*. 4. Before *bhyas*, *hiṃ* replaces *ṅasi* and *ṅas*. 5. Before *su*, *nto* replaces *ṅasi*. 6. Before *ṅas*, *so* replaces *ṅasi*. 7. Before *ṅi*, *em* replaces *su*, *jas*, *ṅasi*, and *ṅas*. 8. Before *sup*, *su* replaces *su*, *jas*, *ṅasi*, and *ṅas*; in these cases, the long vowel is substituted. 9. Before *sup* and *aṅi*, *ṅas* is sometimes elided. 10. Before *śas*, *ṇo* replaces *idut* (words ending in *i* or *u*). 11. Before *ṅas*, *o* optionally replaces *jas*, and the *a* at the end is also elided. 12. Before *caṭā* (consonants other than nasals and semivowels), *ṇā* replaces *asu* (words ending in *as*) and *bhis*; before *sup*, the long vowel is substituted. 13. In the feminine, before *śas*, *ud* optionally replaces *ojas*. 14. Before *am*, the short vowel is substituted for *ṭā*, *ṅasi*, and *ṅas*. 15. For words ending in *id*, *ed*, and *ad*, the *i*, *e*, and *a* are respectively replaced by *ā*. 16. Not so for words ending in *ad* or *āt*. 17. In the neuter, *s* is frequently replaced by *bindu* (anusvāra). 18. Before *jaś* and *śas*, the long vowel is substituted in the neuter. 19. In address (*āmantraṇe*), *s* is replaced by *av*, *uttva* (long *u*), or *bindu*. 20. After *ā*, *e* and *ī* are shortened; after *ṛ*, *āra* is substituted before *sup*. 21. For *mātṛ*, *āu* is substituted before *jas*, *śas*, *ṭā*, and *ṅasi*. 22. For *pitṛ*, *bhrātṛ*, and *jāmātṛ*, *ara* is substituted. 23. From *rājñ* onwards, *ā* is substituted. 24. In address, *bindu* is substituted for *vā*, *jas*, *śas*, *ṅas*, and *ām*. 25. Before *śas*, *ec* is substituted for *ṅas* and *ām*. 26. Before *ṭā*, *ṇā* is substituted for *ṅasi* and *ṅas*, and doubling occurs optionally with the elision of *j*. 27. If not doubled, *ā* is substituted for *ṇo* and *ṇam* before *aṅasi*. 28. For *ātman*, *appāṇo* is optionally used, excluding doubling. 29. Otherwise, it follows the pattern of *rājan* without substitution. 30. Words like *brahman* follow the same rule. 31. For *sarva* and its derivatives, *et* is substituted for *jas* and *ṅi* becomes *ssiṃ*. 32. For *idam*, *etad*, *kim*, *yat*, and *tad*, *iṇā* is optionally substituted for *ṭā*. 33. For *kim*, *yat*, and *tad*, *esiṃ* is substituted for *ām*. 34. For *kim*, *yat*, and *tad*, *āsa* is substituted for *ṅas*. 35. For those [ending in *i*], *ssā* is substituted for *ṅi*. 36. *Hiṃ*, *āhe*, *iā*, and *kāle* are substituted for *ṅas*. 37. *Utto* and *udo* are substituted for *ṅas* except for *idam*. 38. For *tad*, *se* is optionally substituted for *ṅas* even in the feminine. 39. For *āma*, *siṃ* is substituted. 40. For *kim*, *kaḥ* is substituted. 41. For *idam*, *imaḥ* is substituted. 42. Before *ssiṃ* and *sayoḥ*, *aṃ* is optionally substituted for *ṅi*. 43. *Me*, *ne*, and *haḥ* are substituted for *ṅasi*. 44. *Tthaḥ* is not substituted in the neuter. 45. In the neuter, *svam* is substituted for *ṅasi* and *ṅas*. 46. For *idam*, *iṇamiṇamo* is substituted. 47. For *etad*, *so* is substituted for *su*, optionally with *uttva*. 48. For *ṅas*, *tto* is substituted. 49. For *tat* and *tha*, there is elision of *t*. 50. For *tad* and *etad*, *saḥ* is substituted for *su* in the masculine. 51. For *adas*, *do* is substituted for *su*, and *ha* for *ṅas*. 52. *Saupadasya* (of that which has *sau* as its base). 53. For *yuṣmad*: *taṃ*, *tumam*, *tuṃ* for *su*; *am* for *ṅasi*. 54. *Tujjhē*, *tujjha*, *tumhē*, *jas*; *vo* also for *śas*. 55. Before *ṭā* and *ṅi*, *taï*, *taē*, *tumaï*, *tumaē*, *tume*, *tumammi*. 56. Before *ṅasi*: *tumō*, *tuha*, *tujjha*, *tuva*, *tumhāḥ*. 57. Before *ṅi*: *te*, *de*, *tumāi*. 58. Before *bhis*: *tujjhēhi*, *tubbhēhi*, *tumhēhi*. 59. Before *ṅas*: *tatto*, *taïtto*, *tumāō*, *tumāi*, *tumāhi*. 60. Before *bhyas*: *tujjhāhintō*, *tujjhāsuntō*, *tumhāhintō*, *tumhāsuntō*. 61. Before *ām*: *me*, *mama*, *maha*, *majjha*. 62. Before *sup*: *amhēsu*. 63. For *dvi*: *do*, *tī*, *tiṇi* for *jas* and *śas*. 64. For *dvi*: *duvē*, *dōṇi*. 65. For *catur*: *cattārō*, *cattāri*. 66. For these, *ām* is substituted by *ṇhaṃ*. 67. From *śeṣāt* (the remainder), they behave like words ending in *a*. 68. Not so for *ṅi* and *ṅasi*, where *ed* and *ād* are substituted. 69. The dual is treated as plural in the fourth case (*caturthī*). 70. The sixth case (*ṣaṣṭhī*) is treated as the fifth (*pañcamī*). 71. In some instances, it is not for the sake of that (*tādarthye*).
Thus ends the fifth chapter, on the rules for *su*-affixes, in the *Prākṛtasañjīvanī* composed by Śrī Vasantarāja.
[The Sixth Chapter]
[Now the rules for verbal suffixes (tiṅ) are stated.]

In the case of *ta*, *tip*, *id*, *et*, *sip*, *thās*, *si*, *se*, *in*, *mi*, *pō*, *miḥ*, *nti*, *hētthā*, *mō*, *mu*, and *mā* when used in the plural, there is the elision (*lopa*) of *sē* and *astēr*. After *mi*, *mō*, *mu*, and *mānām*, there is the substitution of *haś* for *cayaka*. In the case of *ia*, *ijjaunā*, *antyadvitvēnta*, *māṇau*, *śatr̥*, and *śānac*, as well as in the feminine, [the suffixes] follow the root. In the future tense, *hi* is used. In the first person singular, *ssā* and *hā* are used; in the dual, *minā* and *ssaṁ*; and in the plural, *vāmō*, *mu*, and *maiḥ*. In the case of *hissā*, *hitthā*, *kr̥*, *dā*, *śru*, *vac*, *gam*, *rud*, *dr̥ś*, and *rūp*, the forms are *kāhaṁ*, *dāhaṁ*, *sōcchaṁ*, *vōcchaṁ*, *gacchaṁ*, *rōcchaṁ*, and *dacchaṁ*. For roots beginning with *śru* and others, in all three persons, excluding the nasal (*anusvāra*), there is optionally the elision of *hi*. In the case of *vidhy-ādi* (imperative, etc.), in the singular, *tu* and *ha* are used; in the plural, *mō*. And in the present, future, and non-past tenses, *jja* and *jjā* are optionally used in the middle voice. In the case of non-monosyllabic roots, *īa* is used in the past tense. In the case of monosyllabic roots, *hīa* is used. In the case of *ās*, it is *ēstēḥ*. In the case of *ṇic*, it is *ēd-ādēr ātāvē vā*. In the case of *āviḥ*, it is used in the sense of state (*bhāva*) and object (*karman*). Optionally, *naidāvē* is used. In the case of *ātā*, *mipi* is optionally used. And in the plural, *ic* is used. And in the case of the past participle (*kta*), the infinitive (*tumun*), the gerundive (*tavya*), and the future, there is optionally the substitution of *lā*.
Thus ends the sixth section, the rules for verbal suffixes (*tiṅvidhi*), in the *Prākṛtasañjīvanī*.
[The Seventh Section]
[Now the rules for verbal roots are stated.]

When *bhū* is followed by *ho*, *hu*, or *vaukta*, it becomes *bhava*; *tvar* becomes *tvaras* and *tuvara*; *ghūrṇ* becomes *ghola* and *ghumauna*; *nud* becomes *ṇolla*; *pāṭ* becomes *phāla*; for roots beginning with *vṛṣ*, *ṛt* becomes *ari*; at the end [of such words], *ara* is added; after *kṛ*, *kuṇa* is substituted; after *jrmbh*, *jambha*; after *grah*, *geṇha*; after *chid*, *ghetta* in the forms *ktvā*, *tumun*, and *tavya*. After *kṛ* in the past and future tenses, *kā* is used; after *smṛ*, *bhara* and *sumara*; after *bhī*, *bhāvi* and *ihaum*; after *mlai*, *vā* or *vāatra*; after *tṛp*, *thippa*; after *jñā*, *jāṇa* and *muṇa*; after *ghaṭ*, *gaḍha*; after *sam-lai*, *gala*; after *sraṃs*, *lhasa*; after *ni*, *sada* and *sajja*; after *ā-rabh*, *ḍhava*; after *ud-śal*, *thalla* optionally; after *pib*, *ghoṭa*; after *jalp*, *loma*; after *sthā*, *dhyai*, and *gai*, *ṭhā*, *jhā*, and *gā*; and *ṭhā*, *jhā*, and *gā* are also used in the singular of the future, present, and imperative; after *khād* and *dhāv*, *khā* and *dhā*; after *gras*, *visa*; after *ci*, *ciṇa*; after *krī*, *kiṇa*; after *ve*, *ke* optionally; after *dhmā*, *dhumā*; after *śrad*, *dhō*; after *dah*, *ava*; after *gāh*, *vāha* optionally; after *kāś*, *vāsa*; after *ni*, *māṅ* becomes *māṇa* and *mava*; after *pad*, *vvala*; after *kṣi*, *jhijja*; for the final letter of *bhid* and *chid*, *nda* is substituted; for *kvath*, *ḍha*; for *veṣṭ*, *aut* and *sam* become *lla*; for *rud*, *va*; after *ud*, *vij* becomes *vr̥dh* and *ḍḍha*; for *han*, *mma*; for roots beginning with *ruṣ*, there is lengthening; for *vraj* and *nr̥t*, *ccō* is substituted; for *yudh*, *budh*, *gr̥dh*, *sidh*, and *krudh*, *jjha* is substituted; for *rudh*, *ndha* and *mbha*; for *mṛd*, *la*; for *śad* and *pat*, *ḍa*; for roots beginning with *śak*, reduplication occurs; for *sphuṭ* and *cal*, it is optional; after *pra* etc., *mīl* becomes *mlā*; for roots beginning with *bhuj*, there is elision (*lopa*) in the forms *ktvā*, *tumun*, and *tavya*; for *śru*, *hu*, *ji*, *lū*, and *dhū*, *ṇa* is added at the end and the vowel is shortened; in the passive and reflexive voices, *v* is added; for *gam* etc., reduplication is optional; for *duh*, *lih*, and *vah*, *dujha*, *lijjha*, and *bujjhā* are substituted; for *hr̥* and *kr̥*, *hīra* and *kīra*; for *jñā*, *jāṇa* and *muṇa*; for *grah*, *ghēppa*; with the suffix *kta*, *diṇṇa* etc. are formed; for *takṣ*, *raṃpa* and *vaccha*; for *khid*, *visūra*; for *krudh*, *jūra*; for *carc*, *cara*; for *tras*, *vajja*; for *mr̥j*, *lubha* and *puṃsa*; *buḍḍa* and *khuppa* from *majj*; for *dṛś*, *pulaa*, *ṇiaccha*, *avakkha*, and *saccavā*; for *śak*, *tara*, *vaa*, and *tīra*; and so on for others. The remaining [roots] end in *a*; for those not ending in *a*, *a* is optionally added; substitutions for *aḍ* occur frequently.
Thus ends the seventh chapter, on the processing of the elements (*dhātu-vidhi*), in the *Prākṛtasañjīvanī* composed by Śrī Vasantarāja.
[The Eighth Chapter]
[Now the rule for particles is stated.]

The particles *kīsa* and *kim* are used for inquiry and prohibition; *huṃ* for giving and inquiry; *ccia* and *ccēa* for emphasis; *o* for indication, regret, and alternative; *ira*, *kira*, and *kilā* for uncertainty and narration; *hu*, *kkhu*, *ni*, *ca*, *khu*, *nu*, *jē*, *rāḥ*, *pādapūraṇē*, and *ānantaryē*; *ṇavari* for censure, wonder, and indication; *sukiṇō* for inquiry; *abbō* for sorrow, indication, and conversation; *alāhi* for prohibition; *aï*, *raṇē*, and *vēcca* for address; *dhū* for contempt; *rē*, *arē*, *harē* for address, quarrel, and censure; *piva*, *miva*, *viva*, *va*, and *iva* have the sense of "like" (*ivārtha*); the remaining ones are [to be understood] from Sanskrit.
Thus ends the eighth section, the rules on particles, in the Prākṛtasañjīvanī commentary composed by Vasantarāja.
